'''''Thinopyrum junceum''''', commonly named '''sand couch-grass''', is a species of [[Poaceae|grass]] in the family [[Poaceae]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Thinopyrum junceum (L.) Á.Löve {{!}} Plants of the World Online {{!}} Kew Science |url=http://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:1166962-2 |access-date=2022-07-12 |website=Plants of the World Online |language=en}}</ref> It is found in Europe and temperate Asia, and grows from [[rhizome]]s.<ref>[http://www.kew.org/data/grasses-db/www/imp03472.htm ''Elymus farctus''] at GrassBase - The Online World Grass Flora</ref> They have a self-supporting growth form and simple, broad leaves. Individuals can grow to 52 cm tall.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Thinopyrum junceum (L.) Á.Löve - Encyclopedia of Life|url=https://eol.org/pages/52189834|access-date=2022-02-04|website=eol.org}}</ref>

A relative of [[wheat]], ''Thinopyrum junceum'' is [[salt-tolerant]]. A hybridization of the two creates a salt-tolerant wheat variety.<ref>C.N. Law. New Small-grained Cereals which may have Value in Agriculture. New Crops for Food and Industry. [[International Centre for Underutilised Crops]]. 1989</ref><ref>
{{cite journal|title=A physiologists's approach to improve the salt tolerance of wheat|author1=Gorham, J. |author2=Wyn Jones, R. G. |journal=Rachis|year=1990|volume=9 |issue=2|pages=20–24 |url=http://www.cabdirect.org/abstracts/19921633749.html}}</ref>
